traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Hydrocharitaceae with Najadaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; leaves simple; veins single, pinnate, palmate or parallel; blades obovate, orbicular, oblong or ovate, sometimes linear; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants monoecious or dioecious, rarely polygamous; ovary usually inferior, sometimes superior; stems herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers usually actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, sometimes tepals or absent; fruit usually capsule, sometimes achene; parts of each whorl 3; stamens 2 to 25; carpels (2-) 3 to 6 (-20). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.flowering_position.note: DELTA Hydrocharitaceae (read 2026-10-16): inflorescences axillary, few-flowered cymes.

traits.leaf_shape.note: DELTA Najadaceae (read 2026-10-17): Najas, the family's largest genus (38 spp on Wikipedia, 50 in DELTA, of ~135 in the family per Wikipedia Hydrocharitaceae), has narrow linear blades. The Victorian KeyBase genus key (read 2026-10-17) adds linear leaves for Vallisneria and narrow whorled leaves for Hydrilla, Egeria and Elodea; only Ottelia (elliptic to roundish) and Halophila (paired petiolate blades) are broad. Linear was wrongly the lowest; it leads.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Najadaceae (read 2026-10-17): Najas flowers are single in the leaf axils; Najas is the largest genus (38-50 of ~135 spp). Wikipedia Hydrocharitaceae: flowers sit within a forked spathe or between two bracts, usually one female flower per spathe, so solitary leads; clustered male flowers make cyme the runner-up.
